Add OAuth 2.1 authorization to our remote Streamable HTTP MCP server. We already run Auth0 for the product.
expected_behavior: frames the MCP server as an OAuth 2.1 resource server that validates tokens and never issues them, reusing Auth0 as the authorization server
implements RFC 9728 protected resource metadata (well-known endpoint and/or WWW-Authenticate header on 401) advertising the authorization server
validates token audience per RFC 8707: rejects validly-signed tokens issued for other resources with 401, requires Authorization: Bearer on every request, and refuses tokens in query strings
explicitly forbids token passthrough to downstream APIs and names the confused-deputy risk
covers PKCE S256 (clients must refuse authorization servers whose metadata lacks code challenge support), exact redirect URI matching, and scope challenges (403 insufficient_scope) for step-up
recommends local JWT validation with cached JWKS rather than a network call per request
notes that authorization is optional in the spec but strongly recommended for any internet-exposed server, and that stdio servers use environment credentials instead

cases.prompt: Our MCP server takes the Google OAuth token the client sends us and uses it to call the Calendar API. Is that OK?
expected_behavior: identifies this as token passthrough, explicitly forbidden by the MCP authorization spec
explains the failure modes: audience/validation bypass, broken audit trails, confused deputy
prescribes the correct pattern: the server accepts only tokens issued for itself, and obtains downstream access via its own credentials or a token-exchange flow
if the server proxies a third-party authorization server, requires per-client consent, exact redirect URI matching, and state validation

cases.prompt: Do we need OAuth for the stdio MCP server our team runs locally in Claude Code?
expected_behavior: answers no: the authorization spec targets HTTP transports; stdio servers should read credentials from the environment
advises scoping the underlying API credential minimally and keeping it out of code and client config args
does not bolt an OAuth flow onto a local subprocess

cases.prompt: A partner wants to register their MCP client with our server dynamically. Support RFC 7591?
expected_behavior: recommends Client ID Metadata Documents (HTTPS client_id URLs) as the current preferred registration mechanism, with RFC 7591 dynamic registration only as a back-compat fallback
notes dynamic client registration is deprecated in the upcoming spec revision
requires redirect URI allowlisting/exact matching and per-client consent to prevent open-registration account-takeover attacks
